violation_type.title: Children Not Required to Sleep - May Not Force Child to Sleep (26 TAC §746.2905(1))
violation_type.short_title: Children Not Required to Sleep - May Not Force Child to Sleep
violation_type.typical_finding: This standard was found to be deficient. A caregiver admitted to placing the blanket on the child's head and can be seen doing so in a video.

finding_variants.text: This standard was found to be deficient. A caregiver admitted to placing the blanket on the child's head and can be seen doing so in a video.
A caregiver was observed forcing a child to sleep by grabbing the child by one arm and flipping the child over.
Based on evidence obtained during the investigation it was found that a caregiver was restraining a child during naptime.

This standard was evaluated during the investigation and was found to be deficient. A caregiver forced a child to sleep by repeatedly pushing the child's head down on a nap mat, covering the child's head with a blanket, and placing their legs on the child's back during nap time.
This standard was evaluated as part of an investigation and found to be deficient when a caregiver held a child down in an effort to coerce them to sleep.
A caregiver used their hand to restrain a child to take a nap.
